TikTok video

Fenty Beauty: “What’s in my bag?”

A TikTok promoting the Fenty Gloss Bomb Universal Lip Luminizer. Diverse celebrities ask “What’s in my bag?” and the product stays secret until the end, when the gloss turns out to be what they all share. It brings the brand’s “Beauty for All” message to life.

See moreSee less

The idea

Fenty Beauty’s “Beauty for All” message, shown through its Gloss Bomb Universal Lip Luminizer. The gloss adapts to every tone, style and identity, which makes it a symbol of universal beauty. The video says it without words: you don’t need to fit in to shine, the glow adapts to you.

How I built it

  • The video opens with a montage of diverse celebrities who each look into the camera and ask “What’s in my bag?”.
  • The product stays a mystery until the end. The answer is not a list of luxury items but something they all share: a universal glow.
  • The music comes from an existing Fenty campaign, so the video feels native to the brand. It also carries the viewer from the celebrity voices to the final message.

Why it works

It sells an idea, not just a product. Beauty fans who care about diversity are likely to share it, because it invites them to engage with the concept of universal beauty.

Product concept · moodboard and photos

Jacquemus ‘Les Lumières’

A new Jacquemus fragrance with its own bottle, a campaign moodboard of sunlit Mediterranean scenes (cliffs, lemons, striped towels, long lunches) and product visuals on sand, in a lemon crate and in a straw beach bag.

The idea

A new product concept for Jacquemus: a fragrance called ‘Les Lumières’, with its own bottle design and a campaign built around it.

What the visuals show

Instagram Reel

ESCADA Bali Paradise

A Reel for ESCADA’s Bali Paradise fragrance that follows the journey from harvesting pitahayas to applying the perfume. Made with Giphy Capture and Pexels footage, with a caption and hashtags to match.

See moreSee less

The idea

ESCADA is known for fresh, floral, limited-edition perfumes that elevate femininity. For its Bali Paradise launch (notes of pitahaya, bird of paradise and sandalwood), the Reel takes viewers on a slow, immersive journey through the creation of the fragrance, from harvesting the pitahayas to applying the perfume after getting ready.

Why Instagram

It is the best fit for slow, visually rich storytelling and for showing a fragrance in an aspirational way.

How I made it

  • Giphy Capture: a screen recording that shows the fragrance, taken from ESCADA’s Instagram account.
  • Pexels: all the other footage, by Roman Odintsov.
  • A caption and hashtags to match: “Feel the freshness of Bali in every note…”, #EscadaBaliParadise #TropicalVibes.
TikTok video

Kiko Milano 3D Hydra Gloss

A TikTok presenting three must-have gloss shades, each set against a background that matches its colour and flavour. The aim was to link each product with an emotion and keep the story easy to follow.

See moreSee less

The idea

A TikTok on three must-have glosses from the Kiko Milano 3D Hydra Gloss collection: Candy Rose, Cream Cashmere and Brun Rose. Each one sits against a background that matches its tone and flavour: pink raspberry candy, soft vanilla cream and cocoa brown.

My thinking

I wanted to connect beauty with emotion, so viewers instantly link each gloss with its flavour-inspired visuals and the feeling it represents. Combining the colour palette, the product focus and relatable feelings makes the story both aspirational and easy to follow.

TikTok video

Onitsuka Tiger Mexico 66

A TikTok about how I ended up buying my Onitsuka Tiger Mexico 66, from Pinterest outfit inspiration and brand emails to trying them on in the new Barcelona store. It analyses how consistent brand touchpoints turned my hesitation into a purchase.

See moreSee less

The story

I first bought a yellow pair of Onitsuka Tiger for my boyfriend. I loved how they looked but couldn’t picture myself in them, until Pinterest kept showing me stylish girls wearing them and the brand’s emails kept reminding me of it. When a new store opened in Barcelona, I tried them on in person, found them very comfortable and bought them.

Brand touchpoints

  • Before: Pinterest.
  • During: the new store, Pinterest, email and my boyfriend, who already owned a pair.
  • After: email.

How I told it

The video follows four moments: showing my Onitsukas, scrolling through shoe websites, my boyfriend wearing his pair, and the Barcelona store with a photo of my first day trying them on.

Takeaway

Consistent communication across Pinterest, email and a physical store is what turned my hesitation into a purchase.

YouTube and podcast strategy · moodboards

Rhode: YouTube and podcast

A plan to take Hailey Bieber’s brand Rhode beyond short-form video. A weekly YouTube series covers tutorials, behind-the-scenes stories and dermatologist-led education, and a podcast called Glossed Over builds deeper conversation and community. Both include monetisation ideas.

See moreSee less

The idea

Hailey Bieber’s Instagram and TikTok work well for Rhode, but short, aesthetic-led videos only show the brand’s look quickly. I expanded her strategy to long-form formats to build a deeper connection with the audience.

YouTube: from “aesthetic inspiration” to “trusted beauty educator”

  • Searchable, so it gives Rhode long-term visibility, unlike TikTok’s fast-moving algorithm.
  • It positions Rhode as science-driven and transparent, with experts who build authority.
  • Weekly videos of 8–12 minutes, polished but intimate.
  • Series: tutorials (“How I prepare my skin for the Met Gala”), brand storytelling (“Inside Rhode lab day”) and education (“Dermatologist Reacts: Why Barrier Care Matters”).

Podcast: Glossed Over with Hailey Bieber

  • Builds emotional intimacy and loyalty, and turns followers into repeat customers.
  • Listeners can send questions and voice notes, which creates a community.
  • Weekly episodes of 30–40 minutes, relaxed and conversational. Ideas: “Is clean girl aesthetic a trend or a trap?” and expert interviews with dermatologists.

Monetisation

YouTube: ads, links and sponsored collaborations. Podcast: sponsored episodes and merchandise.

Instagram and TikTok campaign · moodboards

Jaded London × Martina Alguero

A proposal to bring a Jaded London pop-up to Barcelona, a gap in the brand’s world tour, with local micro-influencer Martina Alguero. It includes a get-ready-with-me Reel, a behind-the-scenes TikTok and guest-interview videos, each with metrics to measure success.

See moreSee less

The idea

Jaded London is a Gen Z streetwear brand that sells mostly online. Its planned pop-up world tour covers the US and Asia but no European city, so I proposed a pop-up in Barcelona to reach a wider European audience.

Why Martina Alguero

Known online as Martina Hunter, she is a Barcelona micro-influencer with 26K followers on Instagram and 62.4K on TikTok. She has already worked with Bershka, Adidas and Puma, and her street style matches Jaded London’s aesthetic.

Three pieces of content

  • Get ready with me (Instagram Reel): Martina shows three Jaded London outfits for the pop-up, a format she already posts and Gen Z responds to.
  • Behind the scenes (TikTok): an unfiltered look backstage that makes the brand feel human and relatable.
  • Guest questions (Reel or TikTok): fast-cut interviews with guests (“Describe Jaded London in one word”) that encourage people to post their own content.

How I would measure it

Instagram Insights and TikTok analytics (reach, saves, shares, watch time, comments), follower growth and use of #JadedinBarcelona.

Vogue College Beauty Weekend

A pink palette, both playful and sophisticated, shows brand stands, makeup workshops that build a “Girls Club” community, and shareable moments like fancy drinks and reward games.

The idea

A digital-first concept for Vogue College of Fashion’s Beauty Weekend that raises awareness on Instagram, TikTok and digital ads. It centres on learning, empowering girls, the brands and a fun experience, in a cohesive pink palette that feels playful and sophisticated.

How to read the board

  • Right: the fun side, with fancy drinks and reward-based games that create memorable moments people share on social media.
Instagram audit · photos

Brandy Melville

A short audit of the brand’s Instagram representation, with a mid-size influencer proposed as ambassador to make its content more inclusive and accessible.

See moreSee less

What I found

In Brandy Melville’s recent Instagram posts the casting is very uniform in race, body type and age, there are no visible “expert” roles, and there are no captions, alt text or subtitles.

Three fixes

  • More diverse casting, while keeping the minimalist look.
  • Accessibility tools: alt text, subtitles and higher colour contrast.
  • Real voices: invite customers to share their outfits and shopping experiences.

The ambassador idea

May Ridts, a mid-size influencer whose calm, honest style matches the brand’s coastal look. Weekly try-on hauls, fit guides, live Q&As and accessible content would make inclusion feel natural, not forced.
